thesis: CRAI is overbought and extended (RSI14 74, 7.5% above the SMA20, within about 1% of the 52-week high) with no new catalyst since the Nov 5 earnings, and it is trading against a risk-off tape (QQQ below its 50- and 200-day averages, VIX at the 0.858 percentile). Reward/risk is only about 1.3 even at the pullback entry, so the setup pays little for a stop of about 2.3 ATR. It is a thin, small-cap name (about 122k average shares, 2 analysts, net debt about 207M), so a regime-driven drawdown could gap through levels with poor liquidity. Valuation is not cheap (trailing P/E 27.1, forward 22.9) after the post-earnings run, and the good news is already priced in. Waiting for a deeper pullback or a volume-confirmed break above 217.7 is better than buying now.
